title: Steerable Before Decodable: Multi-Model Causal Evidence of Unembedding-Orthogonal Bottlenecks Beyond the Logit and Tuned Lens

Steerable but Not Decodable: Function Vectors Operate Beyond the Logit Lens (2026). arXiv:2604.02608.
hypothesis: We investigate whether comparative conceptual computations in decoder-only language models operate inside low-dimensional causal subspaces that are strongly steerable layers before becoming decodable through either the Direct Logit Lens, a General-Corpus Tuned Lens (~3,200 diverse scientific text tokens), or a Domain-Trained Residual-Affine Tuned Lens. Across 4 distinct model families and scales (Qwen3-1.7B, SmolLM2-1.7B, Mistral-7B-v0.1, OLMo-2-1124-7B; 1.7B-7.3B), 4 real-world comparative domains, and 2,688 strictly held-out cross-lexicon entity pairs (verified 100% single-token across all four tokenizers), we benchmark Paired-Swap Algorithmic Core Extraction (ACE) against Direct Logit Lens, General-Corpus & Domain Tuned Lens, CAA, L2 Logistic Probes, and random controls using Flip-1D necessity, Keep-1D sufficiency, and free-form multi-token generation steering.

setup.train_test_split: disjoint 8 train / 8 unseen test entities (56 ordered pairs/lexicon x 3 cross-lexicons = 168/domain)
